bullets.title: DeepSeek AI chip development hammers semis; software/cloud extends gains
bullets.body: Reuters reported DeepSeek is developing its own inference-stage AI chip to reduce reliance on Nvidia and Huawei, sending NVDA down ~1.7% and the broader semi complex sharply lower pre-market: MU -4.7%, MRVL -4.6%, AMD -3.7%, WDC -6.1%, STX -5.0%, SNDK -4.4%. Simultaneously, software/cloud names benefited from the 'less Nvidia hardware needed' narrative, with NET +3.4% and NOW +2.8%.

bullets.title: Samsung Q2 profit +19x YoY fails to impress; KOSPI -4.9% triggers circuit breaker
bullets.body: Samsung reported record Q2 operating profit of W89.4T (+1,810% YoY, +56% QoQ) and revenue of W171T, beating buyside estimates of ~W85T, but shares fell ~7% on sell-the-news dynamics after a 382% YTM rally. The KOSPI drop of ~4.9% triggered a market halt, amplifying weakness in global memory and semiconductor names and signaling elevated momentum risk heading into Q2 earnings season.

bullets.title: China restricting overseas access to advanced AI models; US firms shifting to Chinese LLMs
bullets.body: China's Ministry of Commerce and NDRC met with Alibaba, ByteDance, and Knowledge Atlas to discuss making advanced AI model exports a national security matter, potentially restricting overseas access. Simultaneously, US companies ramped use of Chinese AI models (at ~1/20th the price of frontier LLMs) following Anthropic Mythos restrictions — creating an AI sovereignty dynamic that pressures frontier API providers while benefiting infrastructure/sovereign compute plays.

bullets.title: Tech momentum unwind deepening; high-beta basket -13.6% past week, avoid QQQ longs
bullets.body: The high-beta momentum factor basket peaked June 22 at +69% YTD and has since fallen to +31% YTD, down -13.6% in the past week. QQQ realized vol is at the 97th percentile (36.3), 9.3pts above 1M implied (22.9), suggesting the options market is underpricing near-term moves. VXN sits at 27, elevated but below the 30+ danger threshold; gross HF leverage is at the 98th percentile on a 5-year basis with early de-grossing flows emerging.

bullets.title: Market broadening underway: rotation from AI/semis toward Mag7, software, non-AI cyclicals
bullets.body: Multiple strategists (JPM, MS, 22V) flag a regime shift from semis/memory leadership toward Mag7, software, and non-AI cyclicals. Mag7 is trading near 10-year valuation lows vs. SPX, offering a tactical entry. 22V sees S&P 500 CY26 EPS growing +25% YoY to $343 and favors banks, retail, homebuilders, and transports as laggards with asymmetric upside in a normal expansion; earnings estimates are up +23.3% for Q2 with revenue growth of +12.2%.

bullets.title: Rates repricing hawkish: market pricing 30bps of hikes in 2026; 10Y at 4.50%, 30Y above 5%
bullets.body: Jefferies notes the market is now pricing 30bps of rate hikes in 2026 with the 10-year near 4.50% and the 30-year back above 5.0%. UBS formally removed Fed rate cut assumptions and added a 25bps hike assumption for late 2026. Separately, Jefferies flags BEA methodology changes in September could lower measured core PCE from 3.4% to ~3.2-3.3%, creating a near-term inflation optics tailwind even as the structural debate shifts from cost-led to demand-led inflation risk.

bullets.title: Iran Strait of Hormuz attack hits LNG tanker; oil +1.4% but muted macro impact
bullets.body: Iran's IRGC fired missiles at two ships near the Strait of Hormuz, including a Qatari LNG tanker, lifting Brent crude +1.4% and WTI to ~$69.10. Wolfe Research notes the broader Iran oil shock's consumer impact is finishing at the low end of their $50-100bn purchasing power reduction estimate (~$45bn YTD), with gasoline prices falling sharply from peak and providing a potential tailwind for consumer spending in H2.

bullets.title: SpaceX: wall-to-wall initiations (JPM $225 OW, MS $300 OW, GS $205 Buy, Citi $200 Buy, UBS $210 Buy, Mizuho $200 OP)
bullets.body: Five major banks initiated SpaceX (SPCX) coverage simultaneously with Buy/OW ratings and PTs ranging $200-$300, with Morgan Stanley the most bullish at $300 (implying 87% upside from IPO price). Bull cases center on Starship reusability driving launch costs toward $500/kg by 2030, Starlink reaching $247B revenue by 2031, and orbital/terrestrial AI compute at half industry cost per watt. UBS separately flags SpaceX's Terafab semiconductor fab could reach TSMC-scale WFE spending ($50B+/yr) by 2030-31, potentially expanding global WFE to $300B+.

bullets.title: Starlink threatens US cable broadband; MS models 16mn subs by 2030, cable at -3-4% CAGR
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley's 14th Annual AlphaWise Broadband survey shows cable satisfaction at just 46% vs FWA at 63%, with >30% of broadband subscribers likely to switch ISPs in 12 months. MS models ~16mn Starlink broadband subs by 2030 (11% US household penetration) and forecasts cable sub declines at 3-4% CAGR through 2030; CMCSA and CHTR are most vulnerable while TMUS remains the top wireless pick given fastest growth and least legacy exposure.

bullets.title: Memory supercycle intact: Samsung raising DRAM ASPs 20% in Q3; semi industry sales +119% Y/Y
bullets.body: Semiconductor industry sales growth accelerated to +119% Y/Y in May with DRAM up 14% M/M and flash up 26% M/M. Samsung is reportedly negotiating to raise commodity DRAM ASPs by as much as 20% in Q3, and Intel is raising CPU prices by $30-$1,495 across product lines. Morgan Stanley forecasts memory earnings growing 35-40% in 2027 driven by agentic AI ramp; meaningful new supply is unlikely before 2028, supporting the upcycle thesis despite near-term momentum unwind in memory equities.

bullets.title: Banks exploring Fiserv STAR network acquisition; potential Durbin bypass creates regulatory risk
bullets.body: JPMorgan, BofA, Wells Fargo, and PNC are in early talks to acquire Fiserv's STAR debit network to bypass the 2010 Durbin Amendment's debit interchange fee caps, similar to Capital One's Discover acquisition strategy. FISV closed after-hours +6%. Mizuho flags significant regulatory, political, and antitrust hurdles — merchant lobby opposition is likely and prior bank closed-loop attempts (ChaseNet) failed.

bullets.title: Q2 bank earnings setup: strong capital markets/NII, deposit costs rising; UBS adds 25bps hike
bullets.body: Q2 bank earnings previews across UBS, GS, and TD Cowen point to strong NII, investment banking, and trading revenue beats driven by elevated equities activity. C&I lending expected to rise 2.5% q/q per H.8 data. However, UBS removed rate cut assumptions and now models a 25bps hike in late 2026, which will pressure deposit costs. GS identifies FITB, ZION, RF, HBAN, CFG, and KEY as beat-and-raise candidates on loan growth; consumer credit quality is outperforming expectations.

bullets.title: AI infrastructure capex buildout accelerating to $1.2T in CY27; power remains critical bottleneck
bullets.body: Jefferies projects AI-related capex to grow 53% to $1.2T with no near-term letup through CY27, funded in part by $7T+ in AI debt financing projected by 2029. Morgan Stanley flags Google stating it needs to double compute every 6 months (1,000x in 4-5 years), while power-on-demand data center contracts at $10-12/watt with 15-25 year agreements generate 15-19% unlevered FCF yields. Time-to-power stocks (WULF, SEI, VST) have pulled back 10-19% and are flagged as buying opportunities.

bullets.title: Software sector facing structural headwinds; Jefferies underweight app software, favors infra/security
bullets.body: Software is down ~14% over the past year as AI budgets crowd out core software spending and frontier labs risk collapsing traditional software moats. Jefferies maintains underweight on application software, preferring cloud infrastructure, security (up 40-50% past month, near overbought), and token-economics-positioned names. The All-SaaS index trades at 5.3x FY+2 EV/Sales with +6.4% weekly multiple expansion vs. IGV at -14.3% YTD vs. S&P +10.1%.

bullets.title: Gasoline price relief could add consumer purchasing power in H2; lower-income households most delayed beneficiary
bullets.body: Wolfe Research estimates the Iran oil shock cost consumers ~$45bn YTD vs. ~$190bn in fiscal stimulus realized/remaining, finishing at the low end of their $50-100bn purchasing power reduction range. WTI is back near year-ago levels, but gas prices remain double-digit YoY higher across most states and fall slower than they rise. Middle- and upper-income households are the primary near-term beneficiaries; lower-income consumers should see relief as normalization continues, potentially supporting Fed patience.

bullets.title: TSMC PT raised to NT$3,100; datacenter AI CAGR now modeled at 69% through 2029
bullets.body: JPMorgan raised TSMC's Jun-27 PT to NT$3,100 (20x forward earnings, +6% vs. prior NT$2,925) and lifted FY26/27/28E EPS by 5%/10%/16%, driven by near-term gross margins approaching 70% and stronger AI accelerator/CPU demand. Datacenter AI CAGR is now estimated at 69% from 2024-29E. TSMC is expected to push back on market share loss concerns and signal meaningful capacity expansion in 2027-29, with broader price hikes likely in 2027.

bullets.title: Private credit strains not systemic; bank C&I lending accelerating to double-digit growth
bullets.body: Piper Sandler argues private credit stress poses no systemic contagion risk given declining private credit share of GDP since GFC, steady junk bond spreads, and bank C&I loans already accelerating to double-digit YoY growth to absorb displaced private lending. Private credit redemptions also slowed at Blue Owl and KKR FS Income Trust in Q2, easing SaaSpocalypse concerns. Deregulation and looser capital requirements would further enable bank share gains.

bullets.title: META faces $1.4T in state penalties over youth safety; upgraded to Buy at Erste despite risk
bullets.body: Four US states are seeking $1.4T in penalties against Meta over addictive design and youth safety claims ahead of an August trial; Meta denies the claims as unprecedented and unsupported. Despite the headline risk, META was upgraded to Buy at Erste Group and is up 0.3% pre-market, reflecting the market's view that the penalty is unlikely to be imposed at the stated level.

bullets.title: Agentic commerce nascent but card networks well-positioned; grocery/CPG face highest disintermediation risk
bullets.body: JPM retail research frames agentic commerce as currently <1% of web traffic but gaining ecosystem attention rapidly. Card networks (Visa, Mastercard) are well-positioned via tokenization and authentication; PSPs face commoditization risk. Retailers with strong loyalty/data moats (AMZN, COST, ULTA) and proprietary agents (WMT Sparky, HD Magic Apron) are best positioned, while grocery/CPG face the highest disintermediation risk from price-transparent AI agents.

bullets.title: German industrial production +0.9% m/m in May; energy-intensive sectors rising on front-loading
bullets.body: German IP rose 0.9% m/m sa in May, led by cars (+3.6%) and metals (+1.2%), with April revised sharply higher (-0.5% to +0.3%). Energy-intensive sectors (paper, refineries, chemicals, metals) have increased in recent months amid suspected front-loading for US-Iran supply chain risks. EA macro momentum continues to improve following German industrial orders and Sentix survey data, with June Composite PMI rising to 52 (consistent with ~2.7% annualized GDP).
